bib.title: iBOT: Image BERT Pre-Training with Online Tokenizer

question: Can masked image modeling (BERT-style) train Vision Transformers well when the visual tokenizer is learned online jointly with the model rather than pre-trained offline?
hypothesis: A semantically meaningful visual tokenizer is the crux of MIM; self-distilling the teacher's patch outputs, with the teacher semantics from [CLS] cross-view distillation, gives such a tokenizer in a single stage.
contributions: Formulate MIM as knowledge distillation and perform it by self-distillation with the EMA teacher as online tokenizer
Shared projection head and soft token distributions as targets
State-of-the-art k-NN, linear, fine-tuning, semi-supervised, unsupervised and dense-task results
Analysis of emerging part-level patch semantics and robustness
Multi-crop made stable via random MIM; effective-epochs measure

method.summary: Student sees blockwise-masked views, teacher sees unmasked views; loss is cross-entropy between teacher and student softmax outputs on [CLS] (cross-view, as DINO) plus on masked patch tokens (in-view), summed unscaled. Teacher is EMA of student; projection head shared between [CLS] and patch tokens.
method.task: self-supervised image pre-training (masked image modeling + self-distillation), evaluated by k-NN, linear probe, fine-tuning, detection, segmentation

datasets.name: ImageNet-1K
datasets.split: train set for pre-training; val for eval
datasets.preprocessing: 224 size images (196 patch tokens); 2 global crops 224 and 10 local crops 96 (multi-crop)

models.name: DINO, BEiT, MoCov3, SwAV, BYOL, SimCLRv2, EsViT, MoBY

training.objective: L_[CLS] + L_MIM (summed without scaling); cross-entropy self-distillation, symmetrised over two views; blockwise masking; soft teacher distribution
training.epochs: ImageNet-1K: ViT-S/16 800, ViT-B/16 400, ViT-L/16 250, Swin-T 300; ImageNet-22K: ViT-B/16 80, ViT-L/16 50. Tables 1-3 list different 'effective epochs' (e.g. ViT-B/16 1600 = 400 x ~4)
training.regularisation: EMA teacher; centering and sharpening; prediction ratio r=0 w.p. 0.5 else U[0.1,0.5]
training.compute: ViT-S/16: iBOT 2x224+10x96 crops 193.4h for 800 epochs, 19.5G memory (Table 19)

other.momentum rates, temperatures: ablation default patch temp tau't 0.04->0.07, centering momentum m' 0.9, head output K=8192; EMA teacher momentum value not stated in text
other.head: 3-layer MLP, l2-normalised bottleneck, shared between CLS and patch
other.fine-tune ImageNet: BEiT recipe, AdamW, layer decay 0.75/0.65/0.75 for S/B/L, 200/100/50 epochs, lr sweep {8e-4,9e-4,1e-3,2e-3}
other.COCO: Cascade Mask R-CNN, lr 1e-4, wd 0.05, 1x schedule (12 epochs), layer decay sweep
other.ADE20K: 160k iterations, 512x512, layer decay 0.65, lr sweep {3e-5..8e-4}, UperNet or linear

inference.samples: not stated; no seeds or error bars reported
inference.retrieval: k-NN with sweep over number of neighbours (DINO protocol)

eval.protocol: Single run per setting; lr sweeps; no seeds or significance tests reported

results.claim: iBOT ViT-L/16 pre-trained on ImageNet-22K reaches 82.3% linear probing on ImageNet-1K.
results.quote: With ViT-L/16 and ImageNet-22K as pre-training data, iBOT further achieves a linear probing accuracy 82.3%

results.claim: iBOT ViT-L/16 22K pre-trained fine-tuned at image size 512 reaches 87.8%.
results.quote: When ﬁne-tuned on an image size of 512, we achieve 87.8% accuracy.

results.claim: iBOT ViT-B/16 (ImageNet-1K) gets 77.1 k-NN, 79.5 linear and 84.0 fine-tuning.
results.quote: iBOT advances ImageNet-1K classiﬁcation benchmark under k-NN, linear probing and ﬁne-tuning protocols to 77.1%, 79.5%, 84.0% with ViT-Base/16 respectively

results.claim: Gain over DINO in linear probing grows with model size (0.9 with ViT-S, 1.3 with ViT-B).
results.quote: the performance gain over DINO gets larger (0.9% w/ ViT-S versus 1.3% w/ ViT-B) with more parameters

results.claim: MIM without the [CLS] distillation loss gives only 9.5 k-NN and 29.8 linear accuracy.
results.setup: 300-epoch ViT-S/16, r=0.3, no multi-crop, shared head, L_MIM only
results.quote: performing MIM without L[CLS] leads to undesirable results of 9.5% k-NN accuracy and 29.8% linear accuracy

results.claim: Same ablation: BEiT with DALL-E tokenizer gets 6.9 k-NN, 23.5 linear, 81.4 fine-tune; MIM-only fine-tunes 79.4; DINO 80.6.
results.table: Table 9, row BEiT (DALL-E encoder), column Lin.; MIM-only row Fin. 79.4; DINO row Fin. 80.6
results.note: Table 20 reports BEiT linear as 24.2 and k-NN 6.9 (Fin 81.4) for the same setting; Table 9 prints 23.5.

results.claim: Standalone DINO as tokenizer yields 44.3 k-NN against 69.1 for iBOT in the same 300-epoch setting.
iBOT with multi-crop uses 25% more memory and 7.4% more training time than DINO.
results.setup: ViT-S/16, two 8-GPU V100 machines, batch 1024, multi-crop
results.quote: iBOT with MIM induces 25% more memory requirements and 7.4% more actual training time
results.note: Table 19 shows 19.5G vs 15.4G with multi-crop (about 27%) and 13.1G vs 9.3G without multi-crop (about 41%).

results.claim: iBOT is no better than DINO at image retrieval (comparable).
results.quote: iBOT has comparable results with DINO. While iBOT has higher k-NN results on Imagenet-1K, the performance is not better for iBOT in image retrieval.

results.claim: iBOT ViT-B/16 improves COCO APb to 51.2 and APm to 44.2 (DINO 50.1/43.4).
results.setup: Cascade Mask R-CNN, ViT-B/16, 400 epochs, 1x schedule
results.quote: With ViT-B/16, iBOT achieves an APb of 51.2 and an APm of 44.2

results.claim: ADE20K mIoU with UperNet: iBOT ViT-B/16 50.0, +3.2 over DINO.
results.quote: iBOT advances previous best methods DINO by 3.2 on mIoU with UperNet

results.claim: Part-wise probing: top-56 patch tokens, iBOT 5.9 points above DINO; 17.9 with a single token.
results.setup: ViT-S/16 800 epochs, linear on averaged top-k attended patch tokens

results.claim: Soft token distributions help over hard labels (Table 18).
results.note: Value left null: claim only; see Table 18: hardmax 68.1/73.3 vs softmax† 69.1/74.2 (with centering).

results.claim: Text states NMI as 32.8% but Table 5 gives NMI 78.6 and ARI 32.8.
results.note: Text: 'we achieve a 32.8% NMI, outperforming the previous state of the art by 1.8%'; the table column for 32.8 is ARI.

limits: Single runs, no seeds or error bars
Gain from MIM is largest only with the [CLS] distillation loss; MIM alone fails (29.8 linear)
ViT-L/16 on 1K data is 0.4 below BEiT in fine-tuning (84.8 vs 85.2 in Table 2); authors infer iBOT needs more data for larger models
Image retrieval and video object segmentation are not better than DINO
Authors plan to scale to larger datasets and ViT-H/16
Multi-crop without random MIM was unstable

terms.definition: actual pre-training epochs multiplied with a scaling factor accounting for extra trained images of different resolutions induced by multi-crop augmentation
the teacher backbone plus projection head, a visual tokenizer that generates online token distributions for each masked patch token
